                                                                                 1-19.   Monitor Alarm

                                                                                             (D, fig. 1-8)

                                                                                 The monitor alarm provides alarm signals when-
                                                                                 ever a fault is detected in the interrogator set.
                                                                                 These signals consist of a lighted fault indicator
                                                                                 lamp and an audio tone. The monitor alarm may
                                                                                 be mounted in any convenient location which is
                                                                                 within visual and audio range of operating per-
                                                                                 sonnel.

                                                                           1-21. Description of Program Connectors

                                                                                       (fig. 1-12)

                                                                           Program connectors are provided with each con-

                                                                           figuration of Interrogator Set AN/TPX-46(V).

                                                                           These connectors are provided to program the

                                                                           iff set to meet    established           friend

                                                                           admission/enemy rejection criteria. The prog-

                                                                           ram connectors are supplied in three different

                                                                           kits; kit No. 1 is issued with the AN/TPX-46(V)1;

                                                                           kit No. 2 is issued with the AN/TPX-46(V)2,

                                                                           AN/TPX-46(V)3, and AN/TPX-46(V)4, and kit

                                                                           No. 3 is issued with AN/TPX-46(V)6. With the

                                                                           exception of differences in selected programs,

                                                                           the description of the three kits is the same. Kit

                                                                           No. 1 and kit No. 2 each consist of 16 program

                                                                           connectors, of which four have no color code and

                                                                           are never changed; the remaining twelve are

                                                                           divided into three groups of four each. Kit No. 3

                                                                           contains all unique program connectors of kits

                                                                           No. 1 and No. 2, and are used to form kits No. 1

                                                                           or No. 2 as required. The individual groups are

                                                                           color coded, green, yellow, and red and are in-

                                                                           stalled in color groups. The program of the

                                                                           green set provides for the highest enemy rejec-

                                                                           tion, the red provides for a highest probability of

                                                                           friend recognition, and tne yellow provides a

                                                                           median between the pveen and red.

                                                                           ponent used in any other configuration, with

                                                                           the exception of certain cables, the length of

                                                                                                     2-25.  Installation of R-T Group on C-D ©
                                                                                                            Group Case

                                                                                                                (fig. 2-21)

                                                                                                     The r-t group is secured to the c-d group case by
                                                                                                     means of locating keyways, holddown rings and
                                                                                                     holddown straps. To attach the r-t group to the
                                                                                                     c-d group case, proceed as follows.

                                                                                                        a. Depress   the   automatic pressure release
                                                                                                     valve on the   right  side of the r-t group case
                                                                                                     (fig. 2-21).

                                                                                                        b. Remove the front cover of the r-t group by
                                                                                                     first releasing six cover clamps and then remov-
                                                                                                     ing front cover.

                                                                                                        c. Position the r-t group over the c-d group
                                                                                                     case as shown in figure 2-21, insuring that the
                                                                                                     locating keys seat firmly in the keyways.

                                                                                                        d. Separate the two halves of the snap catches
                                                                                                     attached to the holddown straps (fig. 2-22) by
                                                                                                     pulling outward on the catch release rod while
                                                                                                     simultaneously pulling upward on the catch
                                                                                                     handle.

                                                                                                        e. Attach the snaps to the snap rings on the
                                                                                                     c-d group case making sure that the straight side
                                                                                                     of the snaps are closest to the case.

                                                                                                        f. Adjust the length of the straps to permit
                                                                                                     fastening of the snap catch by pulling inward
                                                                                                     on the strap adjusting bar while simultaneously
                                                                                                     applying tension to the strap.

SPIRIT                                                                                                  g. Hold the two halves of the snap catches in
LEVELS
                                                                                                     the relative positions shown in figure 2-21.

                                                                                                     Place the catch retaining rod in the retaining
                                                                                                     rod slot and adjust the straps to a slight ten-
                                                                                                     sion. Press down on the catch handle until the
                                                                                                     catch release rod engages the catch release slot
                                                                                                     as indicated by an audible click. If the tighteningy
                                                                                                     action of the snap catch does not sufficiently
                                                                                                     tension the straps, release the snap catch, tighten
                                                                                                     the strap and refasten the catch.
